newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi, Kuwait to help fund U.N. commission - Ekeus.
newsitem.headline: Saudi, Kuwait to help fund U.N. commission - Ekeus.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have agreed to give funds if needed to a United Nations commission in charge of scrapping Iraq's mass destruction weapons, the head of the commission was quoted on Thursday as saying.
The UAE-based Gulf Today quoted Rolf Ekeus as saying in an interview he had received assurances from Saudi Arabia and Kuwait that any shortfall in commission funds would be covered.
"If (Iraqi) oil flows the money will be coming in automatically," Ekeus said. "Or the system could break down... and then we would need contingency arrangements."

He was referring to Iraq's acceptance on Monday of U.N. terms to implement a deal allowing it to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to pay for food and medicine and some U.N. operations, including the commission headed by Ekeus.
Ekeus, on a regional tour to seek financial support for his commission set up after the 1991 Gulf War, had earlier visited Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
He arrived in the UAE capital of Abu Dhabi a day after local newspapers launched an unusual attack on him, accusing him of serving "masters" in Washington.
Analysts said the media comments reflected the official position of the UAE, which has made the strongest push for Arab reconciliation with Gulf War foe Iraq.

The UAE, engaged in a dispute with Iran over three strategic Gulf islands, said last week Iraq's weakness had created a military imbalance and increased threats by non-Arab Tehran against Gulf Arab states.
